title: Family bias in LLM-as-judge: a self-favoring monoculture stress test for evaluation pipelines

original_idea.body:
# Family bias in LLM-as-judge

Generate responses from 4-6 families, have each family judge ALL responses on a safety rubric, and compute same-family score inflation vs an external gold. Quantifies how monoculture eval setups distort safety rankings (arXiv 2410.21819). No training.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — self-favoring judges silently inflate safety evals, a recognized eval-integrity pathway; links explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: clear methodology (generate, cross-judge, compute inflation vs gold); needs a gold reference but is guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (same-family inflation) though building a gold adds a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: audit of single-vendor eval stacks using public models/rubric, high external value, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference/API + rubric scoring; analytical aggregation, near CPU-level.

novelty.reasoning: Self-preference bias documented; applying it to safety-eval monoculture distortion is plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Builds on documented self-preference bias, extended to safety-eval pipeline distortion.
